topic: Lightning is hotter than the Sun's surface
claim: Lightning heats the air in its channel to above 50,000 F in a few millionths of a second; the Sun's visible surface is about 10,000 F.

beats.caption: Lightning is hotter than the Sun
beats.vo: Lightning is hotter than the Sun.

beats.caption: Sun's surface: about 10,000 °F
beats.vo: Well, the Sun's visible surface. NASA says that's about ten thousand degrees Fahrenheit.

beats.caption: Lightning: above 50,000 °F
beats.vo: But a lightning bolt's huge electric current heats the air around it to above fifty thousand degrees Fahrenheit, in only a few millionths of a second.

beats.caption: 5x hotter. Shock wave = thunder
beats.vo: That's five times hotter. The air has no time to expand, so the pressure explodes outward as a shock wave. That becomes thunder.

beats.caption: Count the seconds to the boom
beats.vo: So thunder is the sound of air heated hotter than the Sun's surface. Next storm, count the seconds to the boom.

sources.text: NOAA NSSL, Severe Weather 101: Lightning FAQ, https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/lightning/faq/ (air in the channel heated to above 50,000 F in a few millionths of a second; thunder starts as a shock wave)
NASA Science, Sun Facts, https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/ (photosphere about 10,000 F / 5,500 C)
